questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the value of $\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{2} \min\{1 - x, 1 - x^3\}\, dx$?
questions.solution:
Let $I = \displaystyle\int_{-1}^{2} \min\{1 - x, 1 - x^3\} \, dx$.

We can rewrite the integrand using the property $\min\{a - b, a - c\} = a - \max\{b, c\}$.

Thus, $\min\{1 - x, 1 - x^3\} = 1 - \max\{x, x^3\}$.

The integral becomes:

$I = \displaystyle\int_{-1}^{2} (1 - \max\{x, x^3\}) \, dx = \displaystyle\int_{-1}^{2} 1 \, dx - \displaystyle\int_{-1}^{2} \max\{x, x^3\} \, dx$

The first integral is simply:

$\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{2} 1 \, dx = [x]_{-1}^{2} = 2 - (-1) = 3$

To evaluate the second integral, we determine the intervals where $x \ge x^3$ and $x^3 \ge x$ by analyzing the sign of $x - x^3 = x(1 - x)(1 + x)$. The roots are $-1, 0, 1$.

In $[-1,0]$, $x^3 \ge x \Rightarrow \max\{x, x^3\} = x^3$

In $[0,1]$, $x \ge x^3 \Rightarrow \max\{x, x^3\} = x$

In $[1,2]$, $x^3 \ge x \Rightarrow \max\{x, x^3\} = x^3$

Now, we split the second integral over these intervals:

$\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{2} \max\{x, x^3\} \, dx = \displaystyle\int_{-1}^{0} x^3 \, dx + \displaystyle\int_{0}^{1} x \, dx + \displaystyle\int_{1}^{2} x^3 \, dx$

$= \left[ \dfrac{x^4}{4} \right]_{-1}^{0} + \left[ \dfrac{x^2}{2} \right]_{0}^{1} + \left[ \dfrac{x^4}{4} \right]_{1}^{2}$

$= \left( 0 - \dfrac{1}{4} \right) + \left( \dfrac{1}{2} -0 \right) + \left( \dfrac{16}{4} - \dfrac{1}{4} \right)

$= $-\dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{2}{4} + \dfrac{15}{4} = \dfrac{16}{4} =4$

Substituting this back into the expression for $I$:

$I = 3 - 4 = -1$

Answer: $-1$
